analysis: The only change in this PR is a one-line documentation addition at docs/provider/cli-reference.md line 1025 (head). It says App Attest serving authorization can remain visible through its unexpired lease, while MDM removal advice requires a matching fresh coordinator decision. The same distinction applies to both doctor summaries, and the line links to ../reference/provider-authorization.md. No code, config, protocol or permission changes are involved. I read both supplied units (head lines 397-1282) for context. The line is consistent with the canonical threat model for TB-011 (A-016, T-053, T-057): a cached lease is not treated as fresh authorization, and premature MDM removal guidance is gated on a fresh coordinator decision. It adds no new attack surface and does not weaken a mitigation. It does not change the receipt policy, revocation behavior, or the authorization boundary, and it removes no documented control. Unchanged surrounding text (logout/revoke, drain, autopilot, fan, addon hold) was not modified, so I did not re-evaluate it as a regression. One unverified point: the linked ../reference/provider-authorization.md was not supplied, so I could not confirm that it contains the cited behavior. That is documentation drift risk only, not a security finding. No threat-model update is needed.
